---
title: "Reference"
subtitle: "Hand-written executable reference + generator-emitted stubs"
---

The production Docusaurus site generates a per-league reference subtree from
endpoint YAML — accurate **schema tables** (`col_name | type | description`).
This Quarto reference demonstrates two complementary approaches:

## 1. Hand-written, executable reference

Two sports are documented by hand. Each function entry carries a **signature**, a
**parameters table**, a **returns table**, and — critically — an **executable
example that renders the real frame** the call produces at build time. That is
the literate-docs guarantee Quarto adds over a static schema table.

- [**MLB reference »**](mlb.qmd) — `espn_mlb_teams`, `espn_mlb_team_schedule`,
  `espn_mlb_team_roster`, `espn_mlb_scoreboard`.
- [**NBA reference »**](nba.qmd) — `espn_nba_teams`, `espn_nba_team_roster`,
  `espn_nba_scoreboard`.

## 2. Generator-emitted `.qmd` stubs

To prove the **codegen → `.qmd`** path (the analogue of the production
`tools/codegen/generate.py --docs`), a small generator
[`_gen_reference.py`](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-py/blob/proto/quarto-docs/docs-quarto/_gen_reference.py)
reads the package's live signatures + docstrings and the endpoint YAML, and emits
one `.qmd` stub per MLB endpoint into `reference/generated/`.

- [**Generated MLB stubs »**](generated/index.qmd)

Run it with:

```bash
cd docs-quarto
python _gen_reference.py
```

::: {.callout-note}
The generator is intentionally small and single-sport: it demonstrates that the
existing endpoint-YAML metadata can target Quarto `.qmd` just as readily as it
targets Docusaurus markdown, so a full conversion would extend the existing
codegen rather than re-author every page.
:::
